about: The rows of the root-motion rate sweep that fail (D123; npm run sweep -- --rates --baseline): each locomotion loop with contacts played at each rate on each body, moved by its root's travel, failing on the sensors' slide or skate past its fail level or no foot that stands still. Keyed `<clip> <body> <rate>`, with its reasons. Each loop that fails a row is answered (D127): its cause, one of `causes`, and why, with the numbers. npm run sweep -- --rates --check fails on a failing row not here or a failing loop with no answer, and reports each row here that passes and each answered loop that fails no row; the baseline may only shrink, rewritten in a commit that says why (--baseline carries the answers of the loops that still fail).

causes.edge-slide: A foot slides along the floor as it lands, before its contact starts, or as it lifts, after it ends, low and slow enough, or close enough to its contact, that the sensors take the slide into its stance. Slow rates stretch it into a long creep; fast ones squeeze the same slide into less time, its skate doubled at 2.
causes.knight-feet: It fails on KayKit's knight alone. The knight's foot is 0.78 of its 406 mm hip height long, its toe 203 mm past the ball (the other five bodies' feet are 0.21 to 0.33 of theirs), and the sensors' levels scale with the hip height (slide 98.2 mm, skate 16.2 cm/s on it): a planted foot's roll under the planter's hold, or a landing's or lift-off's slide, that passes on the other five fails there.
causes.short-contacts: Its contacts hold a foot under a fifth of the cycle, or one foot alone where the motion stands on both (not a hop): for most of the cycle the planter holds nothing, so the unheld feet slide or skate with the motion, or no foot stands at all. No reading core takes holds more of it without moving other clips (D104, D108, D122, D127); the answer names the reading that would, where one exists.
causes.steps-merge: At fast rates two contacts of one foot (a hop's or skip's landings, a jump's, a quick double step) come about 0.1 s apart as played, and the sensors join stances under 0.1 s apart (a foot rolling from heel to toe), so one stance takes the travel between the two contacts as its slide and skate. The planter holds each contact; between them the foot moves as the clip moves it.
causes.stride-varies: A start-stop loop: one step a foot and a pause in a cycle of 1.8 to 2.5 s. Through the pause and the slow steps either side its feet creep along the floor under the sensors' 0.5 H0/s bar for standing, so at slow rates, and at 1 and 1.5 on some bodies, they read a step as a stance and its travel as slide or skate.
causes.swing-stands: At slow rates a foot that shuffles, drags or slides sideways stays within the sensors' band of the floor (4% of H0 to land, 7% to lift) through its swing and under their 0.5 H0/s bar for standing, so they read the swing as standing and its travel as slide, often over the whole cycle. A contact can't hold a foot that is stepping; at faster rates the same swing reads as one.
causes.unheld-step: A foot stands on the floor, as the sensors read it, where the clip's contacts hold none of it: a step or a shuffle the contact reading leaves out, which slides with the motion.
